headline: MacIntyre, Merritt Spark Tennessee Past Penn State 26-20
dek: Tennessee stays unbeaten and atop the power poll while Penn State drops its first game and falls to tenth.
body: With 1:18 left in the fourth quarter and Tennessee clinging to a 26-20 lead, backup quarterback Jake Merklinger faced third-and-35 from his own 4-yard line and uncorked a 51-yard strike to Radarious Jackson that flipped the field and let the Volunteers drain the clock.

Tennessee struck first on a Brad Maddox 38-yard field goal at 11:26 of the first quarter, then surged ahead 11-0 when George MacIntyre hit Joakim Dodson for a 6-yard touchdown and the two-point conversion early in the second. Maddox added a 30-yarder to make it 14-0 before Penn State answered with a Mark Vaughn 3-yard touchdown run at 1:26. Maddox closed the half with a 19-yard field goal for a 17-7 lead. Penn State trimmed the margin to 17-10 on a Yousef Joseph 45-yarder to open the third, but MacIntyre capped an 11-play, 79-yard drive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Braylon Staley for a 23-10 edge. Joseph hit another 45-yarder to cut it to 23-13, then Maddox pushed the lead to 26-13 with a 35-yard field goal at 8:40 of the fourth. Myers found Omari Evans for a 6-yard touchdown at 2:28 to make it a one-score game, but the Volunteers recovered the ensuing onside kick and Merklinger's explosive completion to Jackson iced the outcome.

The box score tells the story: Tennessee outgained Penn State 398 yards to 281, converted 64 percent of third downs to 58 percent, and won the turnover battle 1-0 behind Timothy Merritt's 31-yard interception return of a Myers pass intended for Jay Edwards at 2:38 of the first quarter. MacIntyre finished 21 of 28 for 278 yards and two touchdowns, pushing his season total to 725 yards and keeping him atop the PCFL passing leaderboard. Penn State's Myers threw for 199 yards and a score but absorbed three sacks in the final two minutes, while the Nittany Lions managed just 88 rushing yards on the day. Tennessee's 33:05 time of possession and 4-30 penalty margin reflected the control the Volunteers exerted throughout.

The win moves Tennessee to 2-0 with a two-game winning streak and keeps the Volunteers at No. 1 in the power poll, sitting second in the Eastern Southern behind division leader LSU. Penn State falls to 1-1, drops from No. 1 to No. 10 in the poll, and falls a game behind Texas in the Eastern Atlantic. Next week Tennessee travels to face Ohio State (1-1) while Penn State visits Arkansas (1-1) looking to right the ship.
turningPoint: Merritt's interception at 2:38 of the first quarter gave Tennessee the ball in Penn State territory and sparked the 17-0 run that defined the game.
byTheNumbers: Tennessee 7-of-11 on third down (64%) vs. Penn State 7-of-12 (58%) — the Volunteers sustained drives while the Nittany Lions stalled.
Turnover margin 1-0 Tennessee: Merritt's 31-yard interception return was the game's only takeaway and set up a field goal.
MacIntyre 21-of-28, 278 yards, 2 TD — his 725 season yards lead the PCFL and his efficiency kept the chains moving.
Time of possession 33:05 to 26:55 — Tennessee controlled tempo and limited Penn State's offensive opportunities.

unsungHero.name: Brad Maddox
unsungHero.why: Made all four field-goal attempts from 38, 30, 19 and 35 yards, providing 12 points that proved decisive in a six-point win.
